subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Masala Chai: India's Spiced Tea
description: One-minute skill: Masala Chai: India's Spiced Tea.

hook.text: Masala chai isn't just tea with milk. It's a spiced brew that's inseparable from Indian daily life.

buildup.text: Strong black tea is boiled with milk, sugar, and spices—typically cardamom, ginger, cinnamon, cloves, and black pepper.

discovery.text: The tea is boiled, not steeped. Boiling extracts maximum flavor and creates the thick, creamy texture chai is known for.

twist.text: Indians didn't drink tea until the 1900s. The British-run Tea Board aggressively marketed it to create a domestic market.

climax.text: Today, India consumes 70% of its own tea production. Chai is drunk by 900+ million Indians every single day.

punchline.text: Boiled, spiced, sweet, and milky. Chai is India's heartbeat in a cup.

quiz.question: Why is masala chai boiled rather than steeped?
options: Boiling extracts maximum flavor and creates thick, creamy texture

details.summary: Masala chai is strong black tea boiled with milk, sugar, and a blend of spices including cardamom, cinnamon, ginger, cloves, and pepper. Every family and chaiwala has their own recipe. It is consumed billions of times daily across India, from railway platforms to corporate offices.
details.whyItMatters: Masala chai is India's universal drink, crossing every barrier of class, religion, and region. It is the glue of Indian daily social life.
takeaways: Masala chai is black tea boiled with milk, sugar, and spices
Each family and chaiwala has their own unique recipe
It is consumed billions of times daily across India

faq.question: What is the traditional method for making masala chai?
faq.answer: Boil water with crushed spices, add strong CTC tea leaves and let them boil. Add milk and sugar, bring to a rolling boil, and strain into cups. The boiling method, unlike Western steeping, extracts maximum flavor from both tea and spices. The result is rich, creamy, and aromatic.

faq.question: Why does chai vary so much across India?
faq.answer: India's regional diversity ensures each area has its own chai style. Kolkata favors lighter chai, Gujarat adds lemongrass, Kashmir uses green tea instead of black. Climate, local spice availability, and family tradition all shape the recipe. No single recipe is definitive.
